N.Y. March 6th
1958
Dear Girls.
I came up here for a meting of PAA on the 4th and am staying
over for a meeting of GPU on the 10th - meanwhile engaging in that pleasant
task which Uncle Sam reserves for his nephews of making out my income tax.
In my odd moments will try to give you a brief run down on our
recent trip around So. America.
The Director's flight left I.Y. on the
7th of Feb. with the first stop Havana where Ma and I joined them. We left
there on the 9th and after a four hour flight arrived at Curacoa in the
Dutch B West Indies.
There PAA built a most attractive hotel on the founda-
tion of an old fort which guarded the entrance to the harbor. It was sunday
but they kept the stores open to the delight of the women and dismay of the
men on the trip. On the 10th we made a 72 hour flight across Columbia and a
part of Venzuela to Lima, Peru.
The next morning some of our party flew up
to Cuzco in a Panagra DO3.
We had to tly at 20,000 feet to cross the Andes
and of course in an unpressurized plane we had to have oxygen.
This was
supplied through outlets at each seat and we all wore masks - looking for all
the world like a lot of horses at chow time. Some of the party did not go
because they were worried about the 11,000 feet altitude at Cuzco. To tell
the truth I was too but didn't say anything about it.
Ball when he took delivery of his first airplane he told the pilot to climb
to 10,000 feet.
The pilot objected because they had to make El Paso before
dark but Mr. Ball insisted. The pilot climbed up to 10,000 and coasted on in
to El Paso.
There he asked again why the old man insisted and Mr. Ball said
"I dont mind telling you now.
The doctor said it I went up to 7,500 teet
that I would drop dead so I just spotted him 2,500 feet to prove that he did
not know what the H he was talking about." We loved Cuzco and neither of
us felt the altitude at all. Of course the thing that interested me most was
the stone walls that the old Incas built.
Some of the stones weigh 20 or
30,000 Ibs. were moved as much as a mile and are so close together that you
cant put a knife blade between them at any point of the 7 foot joint.
This
they did without steel chisels - no one knows just how. We stayed overnight
and the next morning flew back to Lima. On the 13th we flew 7 hours along
the coast of Peru and Chili with the unending blue Pacific on our right and
the snow capped Andes on the left. It was a magnificent flight. we spent
that night and the next in Santiago and on the 15th lew over the nigest
mountain in this hemisphere and then cireled down in a valley to 15,000 feet
where we had a good look at the Christ of the Andes. After about three hours
we landed at Bariloche in the Chilean Lake country. Actually we were just
over the Chilean border in Argentina some 450 miles south and west of B.A.
The lake was something like Lake George - the water as blue - but the mount-
ains all around were rougher, higher and mostly snow capped. We were there
of course in their summer.
At the little hotel where we stayed Mr. Trippe
had us all in a little room off the bar for drinks before dinner.
Someone
tapped me on the shoulder and when I turned around there was wes shapleigh.
The Ss, Danforths, Stuarts and Whitesides all old friends from St. Louis
were on a trip around South America.
It was as though you'd run into an old
friend at Lake Pharoah.. Frank Gledhill and I got up early the next morning
and went fishing.
We were only out about an hour but he caught an & lb.
rainbow trout. we had lunch at a private home on the edge of the lake which

reminded us a 10t of the le Caus at be only much nore of it and on a
grand style.
From there ve drove to the airport and after a perfectly
beautiful flight over the lakes and the pampas arrived in Bed• late in the
afternoon. It wes carnival time and all the shops were closed - a circum-
stance which some of the ladies in the party were unkind enough to say had
been so plenned by those men who made out the itinerary! The second evening
we were all invited to meet the President et the Palace.
General Arenburu
is a fine looking man who was one of those responsible for throwing out
Peron and has ruled the country very well ever since. He refused to run for
the presidency on the sound conviction that if he did so the world would
conclude that free elections in the Argentine were a fraud. Frondizi who
was elected after we left is not well regarded and if he doesn't behave you
may see Gen. Aremburu come off the bench and start pitching again.
We left Beh. on the 19th and flew along the valley of the Platte
for 2) hours when we arrived at Ascuncion capital of Paraguay. It is a sicep
old indian city which probably looks about like it did several hundred years
ago except for quite a lot of dilapadated autonobiles. we were received at
the so called Palace by the resident who has recently been "elected" for
another term. (le was the only cendidate.) He wae a touch friendly men and
I suspect just what the country needs.
we left the same afternoon and after
another 2) hours flight in our special PAA DC arrived at the fabulous city
of Seo Paulo or sto Paul. The difference between Sao Paulo and Rio is about
as the difference between st. louis and Houston. A group of go-getters have
brought to seo Paule branch plants of General Hotors, Chrysler, Pord, Hercedes
Benz and hundreds of other manufacturers.
while it is the colfee capital of
the world it is more importent now as an industrial city.
They claim that
during day 1ight hours a new building is completed every
twenty minutes. I
counted from our twenty story hotel room 18 sky scrapers in one or another
stage of construction.
The population has grown from 50,000 filly Jears ago
to more than 3,500,000
Real estate values or at least prices are higher
than New Yorke
Ine next day leb. 20th we took an hour to fly to itio where we
cireled the city with its magni ricent harbor - over sugar loaf with ita cable
car which I have never riden and dont intend to.
The next day we men drove
up to the sumer capital of Petropolis Ior a meeting with the President. He
is a fine looking man whose ambition is to move into the new capital before
his term expires in 1961.
We left ido on the 22 for that capital - Brezilia
some 400 miles north of lio. it is amazing.
with no water transport, no
reil road and the roughest kind of a highway they are building a new capitol
from scratch. Most of the building materials have been flown in.
The land-
ing strip is 21,000 feet long so that jet planes can use 10,5008 to land,
discharge their passengers and use the other 10,500• for twiceoff.
The adain.
istration building is nearing completion as is a hotel.
the rest is just
dust and vacant land. We left there in the late afternoon and flew over
dense jungle and the
Amazon to arrive some seven hours later at son Juan,
Puerto idea. There we stayed in a new hotel built by PAA.
Early in the
morning of the 23rd we made the short one hour flight to Cided Iridillo in
the so called Republic of San joningo. The "Generalissino" put on a very
swank party for us at the Palace with wonderful burfet dinner and a sym hony
orchestra.
We had to first walk down a long receiving line headed by the
generalissimo and then we had to get in line and snake hands in turn with
a long line of people.
Our old China friend 3111 Pawley is now hand and
glove with trujillo helping run the country if you can believe B1l1. lle is

drilling for oil, handlin sundry negotiations for Irujillo etc. Anyway
it was a lot of fun to see him again.
He looks ten years older than when
1 last saw him and certeinly is far from robuste He said the Generaliasimo
in a talkative mood once told him "you nordic people are not like us latins
you have on election campaign during the course of which each aspirant
calls the other every kind of a crook and imbicile but when one wins they
shake hands and thate the end of it.
however with us latins the man who
gets licked immediately starts plotting to over throw the government and
so often suceeeds that the crowd which wins steals everything in sight know-
ing that they wont be around very long."
Trujillo has been running the show
in San Domingo for 25 years or more and has really done a job. They have
more schools per capita then we, more hospital beds, education 1s cunpul-
water suppiy, tine roads run everywhere and cidad Trujillo is the cleanest
city in the world.
we lert sen Domingo on the morning of the 24th flew over count-
less islands surrounded by that crystal clear water so characteristie of
that section with miles and diles of beaches over luthers and Nasau on in
to patrick Air Force Base just south of Cocoa, Ploride. Ihere the ladies
were entertained by their local counterparts while the men all of whom had
heir 1002.
been cleared for "top secret" received a briefing - very well done - and
then went to Cape Canaveral.
They are so particular about that teat ronge
that I wont say anything except that it was most interesting.
PAA is play-
ing an importent part which the Commanding General very graciously acknow-
Ledged.
The main party
left around seven P.M. for liew Tork while
the Gledhills and Bixbis flew in Wilbur Norrison's DO3 to Miand and then
Ma and I continued on alone in the DC3 to Port Myers.
one sad note. At Santiago, Chill Krs.
Bob Fleming wife of
the Chairman of the Riggs Bank in Washington who has been on many of these
trips with us sa had a stroke from which she never regained conciouness.
Bob stayed with her in Santiago and brought her body back to Washington.
The captain of our ship was an old Pacific pilot who you
may remember Capt. Vinal.
We had two most attractive Stewardesses, a
Purser who was very good. A First Officer and a flight engineer completed
the crew. The Directors were the Trippes, Leslies, Gledhills, Mc Kees
she is a new wife who calls herself an Hawaiian but she looks Chinese)
Levis's, Howards, Ingells, Chandlers, Hemils, Henry Friendly and Admiral
McDonnel the latter two without wives.
After a trip around the world in January and around so.
America in Zebuary 1 would like to confine my further travels to the
Kinsey boat line between Captiva and the mainland but will have to make
some more trips to NoY.
Lots of love
properties.sfomuseum:description: Typewritten letter from Harold M. Bixby to his daughters, dated March 6, [1958], in New York; includes description of Board of Directors tour of South America from February 7 to the 24th beginning in New York with stops in Havana, Lima, Santiago, Buenos Aires, Ascension (Paraguay), Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Brasilia, San Juan, Ciudad Trujillo, Cocoa Beach (Florida), and New York.
